beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its lord, Daran Veyr, argues that distant calculations conceal local deterioration.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An inspection brings the family toward needs that official records may misrepresent.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The journey widens the novel from one household to a contested civilization.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Food, recognition and authority become inseparable questions along the route.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book gives you grounds for suspicion without making every accusation proof.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Who benefits from a crisis remains a question to investigate through reading.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One recurring question is whether protecting someone also grants power over their choices.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Sava wants Taren alive, yet he resists the terms of that protection.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Institutions make similar arguments when they define acceptable lives for whole populations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The resemblance does not make family care identical to government coercion.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It shows how familiar reasons can acquire different consequences at different scales.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: As a reader, you can follow that shift across conversations, procedures and public acts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel's ethical pressure comes from keeping those scales in view together.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel follows consequences across years, rather than ending with one dramatic incident.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its five parts widen from sheltered peace toward the institutions that follow crisis.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A gesture can become a symbol, and a practical response can become a rule.
